absent: Full layouts of network device, transmit queue and packet structures beyond referenced fields
Valid call contexts, sleep and interrupt rules for queue and address locks
Trigger conditions and ordering for registration state transitions
Meaning and assignment of individual message enable category bit positions
Selection conditions for alternative ownership and more flag builds
Driver transmit operation contract beyond success versus other return handling shown
Hardware address sync helper behavior and error cases
Upper and lower adjacency list ownership and lifetime rules

findings.text: A device carries a message enable mask. Each logging category is represented by one distinct single bit derived from a per category bit position. Dedicated predicates test whether a given category is enabled for a device. Categories cover driver, probe, link, timer, interface down, interface up, receive error, transmit error, queued transmit, interrupt, transmit completion, receive status, packet data, hardware and wake on lan.

A debug level initializer maps a small integer to an enable mask. Negative or excessively large level yields a caller supplied default, zero yields silence, and other levels yield a mask with that many low bits set.

Each transmit queue has a dedicated transmit lock and an owner marker. Normal, bottom half disabled and try acquisition record the acquiring processor, while releases clear the marker before dropping the lock. Ownership can be tested against a processor number, with concurrent changes by other processors limited to clearing or recording their own identity.

Hard transmit locking is conditional on the device lockless transmit flag. Non lockless devices use the queue lock primitives, while lockless devices use pairing acquire and release annotations without taking the lock. There are lock, try lock and unlock forms, plus device level bottom half disabled wrappers.

Disabling device transmission serializes against queue state with a global device transmit lock and bottom half suppression, then walks every transmit queue, takes its queue lock, marks that queue stopped, and releases the queue lock before dropping global serialization.

Address list protection uses a dedicated device address list lock with plain and bottom half disabled forms. The lock operation supports a nesting level taken from the device when lock dependency tracking is active, otherwise zero.

Transmit timestamp state is refreshed to current time. One form skips devices marked lockless transmit, another refreshes only when the stored value differs from now, and a device level helper applies the conditional refresh to the first transmit queue.

Device allocation helpers provide single queue and symmetric multi queue creation in terms of a common multi queue allocator with separate transmit and receive queue counts. The single queue form requests one transmit and one receive queue, while the multi queue form requests the same caller supplied count for both directions.

Hardware address assignment uses the length stored in the device when delegating to a lower level setter. Unicast and multicast list synchronization delegates to shared hardware address sync helpers operating on the respective device list, passing through driver sync and unsync callbacks and returning the sync outcome.

Nested synchronization uses two single bit flags for immediate and pending work, derived from dedicated bit positions. A small holder pairs a flag byte with an opaque pointer for per traversal private state.

Upper and lower device adjacency can be walked with iterator macros. Upper traversal uses a read copy update safe next accessor. Lower traversal offers device and private pointer forms, each with a normal and a read copy update safe variant driven by list state.
Receive side scaling key length is 256.
Bonding information pairs slave state with master state. A notifier wrapper places a generic notifier info header first, followed by the bonding information payload.

Checksum offload suitability depends on requested protocol and device features. Fibre channel over Ethernet needs its dedicated cyclic redundancy feature. Generic hardware checksum accepts everything else, internet protocol version four and six need their respective checksum features, and other protocols are rejected.

Hardware timestamp retrieval prefers an optional driver operation when present, otherwise it returns the hardware stamp already associated with the packet. The driver override receives the device, the shared hardware stamp state and a cycle versus time selector.

The transmit more hint has two build dependent storage disciplines, one using per processor soft network state and one using per task transmit state. Each discipline provides paired set and query operations with identical logical behavior.
Transmit entry publishes the more hint then invokes the driver transmit operation. A queue aware wrapper additionally refreshes queue transmit time only when the driver reports success.

Feature intersection preserves only features common to both inputs, except that a mismatch on generic hardware checksum expands the generic side to include internet protocol checksum features before intersecting. Wanted features keep non hardware controlled current features and add requested hardware features. Segmentation offload growth delegates to a feature increment helper with full segmentation and linked feature sets constrained by a mask.

Segmentation suitability maps a packet segmentation type to the corresponding device feature bit and requires all mapped bits to be present, with fixed identifier variants normalized first. Packet level suitability also requires fragment list support when the packet carries a fragment list. A separate need check requires segmentation state plus either unsuitable offload or an unexpected checksum state.

Receive aggregation and segmentation maximum sizes are selected by packet protocol, using the internet protocol version six limit for version six packets and the internet protocol version four limit otherwise. Reads follow the single access discipline paired with the corresponding size setters.

Device role predicates test private and general flags to identify media access security, macvlan and macvlan port, bond master and slave, no frame check sequence support, layer three handler, master and slave, bridge and open switch master and port and their unions, team master and port, link aggregation master and port unions, and failover and failover slave. A scope identifier helper returns the interface index for layer three slaves when that configuration is active, otherwise zero.

Destination retention clears both transient and permanent destination release flags. Virtual local area network maximum transmission unit reduction currently holds exactly for media access security devices.

Registration progresses through uninitialized, registered, unregistering, unregistered, released and dummy states, each with a distinct human readable suffix, with unknown values warned about once. Device naming falls back to a placeholder when the name is empty or still contains a format placeholder.

Device warning helpers emit a device warning that prefixes caller supplied text with the resolved device name and registration state suffix, in once and repeated forms. A module alias helper builds a network device alias string from a device name.
Packet type hash table has 16 entries, with a mask one less than the size.
Device statistics fields are manipulated through atomic long helpers that increment, add a value, or read the stored counter for a named field.

Transmit recursion state holds a recursion counter and a more flag, with additional optional members depending on build configuration for egress queue skipping, action redirect nesting including a bounded device stack, and netfilter duplicate recursion depth.
Action redirect nesting limit is 4.
A filter verdict decoder extracts the embedded error by shifting away verdict qualifier bits and negating the result.
Ethtool event notification and receive checksum fault reporting are provided as empty operations in these fragments, accepting a device and command or packet but performing no observable action.

Two alternative definitions exist for transmit ownership testing and for transmit more storage. One ownership form compares the recorded owner against a processor number, the other compares real time lock ownership against the current task. Consumers must not assume which storage or ownership discipline is active without knowing the selected build configuration.
